questions.title: AND keeps shared one bits
questions.description: Evaluate 1100 AND 1010, treating each string as a four-bit binary value.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Compare the two operands column by column; a result bit is one only when both bits are one.
questions.explanation: Only positions set in both operands remain: 1000₂, which is 8.

questions.title: OR combines set bits
questions.description: What decimal value results from 0101 OR 0011?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Mark each position that contains at least one one.
questions.explanation: The OR result is 0111₂ because a position is set when either operand has a one.

questions.title: XOR with an identical value
questions.description: What is 1010 XOR 1010?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: XOR is one only when the two bits differ.
questions.explanation: Equal bits XOR to zero, so a value XOR itself is zero.

questions.title: XOR two small values
questions.description: Compute 6 XOR 3 in decimal.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Write both values in binary before comparing bit positions.
questions.explanation: 6 is 110₂ and 3 is 011₂; their XOR is 101₂, or 5.

questions.title: Complement of a Java int
questions.description: What does Java evaluate for the int expression ~5?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Remember that Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation.
questions.explanation: For signed two’s-complement integers, ~x equals -x-1; therefore ~5 is -6.

questions.title: AND of decimal values
questions.description: Evaluate 12 & 10 using Java integer bitwise AND.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Convert both decimal operands to binary.
questions.explanation: 12 is 1100₂ and 10 is 1010₂; AND leaves 1000₂, which is 8.

questions.title: XOR cancels paired values
questions.description: A value x is XORed with itself. What value remains, regardless of x?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Use the identity x ^ x = 0.
questions.explanation: Every bit is equal to itself, so every XOR result bit is zero.

questions.title: Zero OR a value
questions.description: For any int x, what does x | 0 return? Answer with the preserved operand.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: At every position, OR with zero keeps the other bit.
questions.explanation: OR with zero leaves every bit unchanged, so the expression evaluates to x.

questions.title: Bitwise operator precedence
questions.description: In Java, evaluate 5 | 2 & 1. Bitwise AND has higher precedence than bitwise OR.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Apply & before |, then evaluate the resulting bit patterns.
questions.explanation: First 2 & 1 is 0; then 5 | 0 remains 5.

questions.title: Ones in a negative int
questions.description: How many one bits are in the Java int value -1?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: The question specifies a Java int, whose width is 32 bits.
questions.explanation: In 32-bit two’s-complement form, -1 has every bit set.

questions.title: Shift left once
questions.description: What value is produced by 6 << 1?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: A left shift by one moves every bit one position toward higher significance.
questions.explanation: For this positive value, shifting left one place multiplies by two: 6 becomes 12.

questions.title: Unsigned shift right
questions.description: Evaluate 20 >>> 2 for a positive Java int.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: For positive values, >>> and >> both shift in zero bits at the left.
questions.explanation: 20 is 10100₂; moving its bits right twice yields 00101₂, or 5.

questions.title: Create a one-bit mask
questions.description: What decimal value does 1 << 3 produce?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: The shift count is the bit position of the one.
questions.explanation: Shifting the value one left by three positions creates binary 1000₂, which is 8.

questions.title: Oddness from the low bit
questions.description: What is the result of 13 & 1?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: The mask 1 isolates bit zero.
questions.explanation: 13 is odd, so its least significant bit is one and the AND result is 1.

questions.title: Set a selected bit
questions.description: Set bit position 2 of value 8, with positions numbered from zero. Return the resulting decimal value.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Create the mask for position 2, then OR it with the value.
questions.explanation: The mask 1 << 2 is 4; 8 | 4 sets that bit and gives 12.

questions.title: Clear one selected bit
questions.description: Clear bit position 1 of 15, numbering positions from zero. Return the decimal result.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: AND with the complement of 1 << 1.
questions.explanation: 15 is 1111₂; clearing position 1 leaves 1101₂, which is 13.

questions.title: Toggle the low bit
questions.description: Toggle bit position 0 of 10. What decimal value results?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: XOR changes exactly the positions selected by the mask.
questions.explanation: 10 is 1010₂; XOR with 1 toggles its low bit to produce 1011₂, or 11.

questions.title: Mask the lowest four bits
questions.description: What decimal value is left by 0b101101 & 0b001111?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: The mask has ones only in positions zero through three.
questions.explanation: The mask retains the lowest four positions: 1101₂, which is 13.

questions.title: Java int shift distance
questions.description: For a Java int, evaluate 1 << 34. Java uses only the low five bits of an int shift distance.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: An int shift count is reduced modulo 32.
questions.explanation: 34 & 31 equals 2, so Java evaluates 1 << 2, which is 4.

questions.title: Test bit five
questions.description: Is bit position 5 set in decimal value 41? Answer true or false.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
questions.explanation: 41 is 101001₂; bit 5 is one, so the masked test is nonzero.

questions.title: Check an even number
questions.description: A program tests (n & 1) == 0. For n = 42, what does this test return?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Even integers have a zero in bit position zero.
questions.explanation: 42 is even and its lowest bit is zero, so the comparison is true.

questions.title: Power of two check
questions.description: Does the positive integer 64 satisfy (n & (n - 1)) == 0?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: The standard check also requires n > 0; here n is positive.
questions.explanation: A positive power of two has one set bit; subtracting one clears it and sets lower bits, making the AND zero.

questions.title: Clear the lowest set bit
questions.description: Evaluate 12 & (12 - 1).
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Subtracting one flips the lowest one and the trailing zeros.
questions.explanation: 12 is 1100₂ and 11 is 1011₂; the AND is 1000₂, or 8.

questions.title: Find the unpaired value
questions.description: In [4, 1, 4, 7, 1], every value appears twice except one. What value remains after XORing the list?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: XOR is associative and a ^ a equals zero.
questions.explanation: The repeated 4s and 1s cancel in XOR, leaving 7.

questions.title: Count set bits manually
questions.description: How many one bits are in binary 1101?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Count the one digits, not the binary numeral’s length.
questions.explanation: 1101₂ contains ones in positions 3, 2, and 0, for a total of three.

questions.title: Isolate the lowest one bit
questions.description: For positive x = 40, what decimal value is x & -x?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: The identity x & -x isolates the least significant set bit.
questions.explanation: 40 is 101000₂; its lowest set bit is 001000₂, which is 8.

questions.title: Java population count
questions.description: What does Integer.bitCount(29) return?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Convert 29 to binary, or count its set positions.
questions.explanation: 29 is 11101₂ and contains four one bits.

questions.title: Reject zero as a power of two
questions.description: A check is n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0. For n = 0, what is the final boolean result?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: A power-of-two test must exclude zero explicitly.
questions.explanation: The first condition, 0 > 0, is false, so the conjunction is false.

questions.title: Find a missing value with XOR
questions.description: The values are [0, 1, 3, 4], drawn from the complete range 0 through 4. Which value is missing?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Use that each value appears once in the range and once in the list except the missing one.
questions.explanation: XORing the full range with the present values cancels 0, 1, 3, and 4, leaving 2.

questions.title: Recover two odd-frequency values
questions.description: In [1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 4], exactly two values occur an odd number of times. Return them in ascending order as a JSON integer list.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: XOR all values to separate the two unique values by a differing set bit.
questions.explanation: The paired 1s and 2s cancel; the odd-frequency values are 3 and 4.

questions.title: Count all subsets by masks
questions.description: How many subsets can be represented by bitmasks for a set of three distinct elements?

examples.input: Three elements; one bit per element

constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Each element contributes one independent binary choice.
questions.explanation: Each of three positions can be absent or present, giving 2^3 = 8 masks.

questions.title: Decode selected indices
questions.description: Mask 1010₂ represents selected zero-based indices. Return those indices as a JSON integer list in ascending order.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Read the bit positions from right to left starting at zero.
questions.explanation: Bits one and three are set in 1010₂, so the selected indices are 1 and 3.

questions.title: Check membership in a mask
questions.description: Mask 10110₂ represents a subset. Is element index 2 present? Answer true or false.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
questions.explanation: Bit two of 10110₂ is one, so the element is present.

questions.title: Decode a small subset
questions.description: Mask 101₂ selects positions from zero. Return the selected positions as a JSON integer list in ascending order.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Associate each binary digit with its zero-based bit position.
questions.explanation: The rightmost and leftmost bits are one, selecting positions 0 and 2.

questions.title: Count submasks including zero
questions.description: How many submasks does 101₂ have when the enumeration includes zero and the mask itself?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Only the set bits of the original mask can vary.
questions.explanation: The mask has two set bits, so each can be included or omitted: 2^2 = 4 submasks.

questions.title: Choose two from five
questions.description: How many distinct subsets of size two can be selected from five distinct elements?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Count unordered pairs; swapping the two selected elements does not make a new subset.
questions.explanation: There are 5 choose 2 = 10 such subsets.

questions.title: Build a selection mask
questions.description: Starting with mask 0, set positions 1 and 4. What decimal mask results?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Set both requested positions with OR.

questions.title: Remove a selected item
questions.description: Mask 1101₂ records selected indices. Clear index 2 and return the decimal mask.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Use mask & ~(1 << 2).
questions.explanation: Clearing bit two changes 1101₂ to 1001₂, which is 9.

questions.title: Subsets containing a fixed item
questions.description: How many subsets of six distinct elements contain one particular required element?

examples.input: Six elements; one specified element must be present

constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Fix the required element, then count choices for the remaining elements.
questions.explanation: Once the required element is included, each of the other five elements is independently optional: 2^5 = 32.

questions.title: Total submask-loop work
questions.description: Across every mask of four bit positions, a loop visits all submasks of each mask, including zero. What is the total number of visits?

examples.input: sum of submask counts for masks 0 through 15

constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Count mask/submask pairs independently for each bit.
questions.explanation: Across all masks, each bit can be absent from the mask, absent from its submask, or present in both: 3^4 = 81 pairs.

questions.title: Single value among pairs
questions.description: In [9, 3, 9, 2, 3], every value occurs twice except one. Which value remains after XOR cancellation?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: XOR each element once; paired values disappear.
questions.explanation: The two 9s and two 3s cancel, leaving 2.

questions.title: Trace a short XOR reduction
questions.description: Evaluate 1 ^ 2 ^ 3 ^ 4 from left to right.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Use associativity and cancel equal pairs.

questions.title: Toggle one bit in a mask
questions.description: Toggle bit position 2 of mask 0111₂. Return the decimal result.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: A set bit in the XOR mask toggles the corresponding original bit.
questions.explanation: XOR with 0100₂ flips that bit off, leaving 0011₂, or 3.

questions.title: Encode two permission flags
questions.description: A permission mask sets zero-based flags 1 and 4. What is its decimal value?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Build the mask by ORing the two one-bit values.
questions.explanation: The set bits contribute 2^1 + 2^4 = 2 + 16 = 18.

questions.title: Count bits in a byte pattern
questions.description: How many set bits are in 255 when considered as an 8-bit value?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: The binary representation of 255 fills one byte with ones.
questions.explanation: 255 is 11111111₂, so all eight bits are set.

questions.title: Check whether masks are disjoint
questions.description: Masks a = 1010₂ and b = 0101₂ select no common positions. Does (a & b) == 0 evaluate to true?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: An AND result of zero means there is no shared set bit.
questions.explanation: The set positions do not overlap, so their AND is zero and the test is true.

questions.title: Find the missing value from a range
questions.description: Values [0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7] contain every value from 0 through 7 except one. Which value is missing?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Each present value appears once in both XOR groups.
questions.explanation: XORing the complete range with the provided values cancels every value except 3.

questions.title: Apply a sequence of mask updates
questions.description: Start with mask 0. Set positions 1 and 3, then clear position 1. What decimal mask remains?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Track the mask after each operation rather than combining them mentally.
questions.explanation: Setting the two positions makes 1010₂; clearing bit one leaves 1000₂, or 8.

questions.title: Maximum XOR pair
questions.description: For values [3, 10, 5, 25, 2, 8], what is the maximum XOR obtainable from any pair?
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: Compare high-order bits first; a trie or greedy prefix test is a common strategy.
questions.explanation: 25 XOR 5 equals 28, and no pair in the list yields a larger XOR.

questions.title: Answer a prefix-XOR range query
questions.description: For array [3, 1, 6, 4], compute the XOR of inclusive indices 1 through 3.
constraints: Assume Java int uses 32-bit signed two’s-complement representation unless the prompt specifies another width.
hints: XOR the selected range, or use prefixXor[right] ^ prefixXor[left - 1].
questions.explanation: The requested values are 1, 6, and 4; 1 ^ 6 ^ 4 equals 3.
